paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend. David doesn't become king because he's the loudest or the strongest. The people come to him and say the LORD told him, "You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them." (1 Chronicles 11:2) They anoint him "according to the word of the LORD through Samuel." (1 Chronicles 11:3) God's word came first, and everything else followed it.

Then the people of Jebus tell David, "You will never get in here." (1 Chronicles 11:5) Friend, I know that sound. I lived in the back of a junk drawer where everybody figured I was done, and the dust agreed with them. But "never" is a big word to say to a man the LORD has already spoken over, and David captured the fortress anyway. When God has said something, somebody else's "never" doesn't get the last word.

Look at how the passage ends: "And David became greater and greater, for the LORD of Hosts was with him." (1 Chronicles 11:9) It doesn't say it was his army or his plans. The reason is the LORD of Hosts being with him. So, baker, when you open the Word today, don't ask how big you are. Ask who is with you, and stay close to Him.
